text:
COP fell 1.6% today to $127.30, continuing a sharp week-long slide as geopolitical tensions that had supported oil prices eased. U.S. crude dropped nearly 8% last week after Iran and the U.S. held talks at the UN, with Iran proposing a conditional ceasefire—the opposite direction from what energy stocks need to rally. Though the Trump administration just rejected Iran's offer and signaled renewed military action after midterms, the initial market relief from diplomatic engagement has weighed on oil and refiner valuations already.

The broader pressure is deeper: U.S. oil sits at $96.41 per barrel while world prices are at $114.89, a wide gap that typically squeezes refiner margins and makes domestic producers less competitive globally. With crude down from higher levels and geopolitical risk temporarily off the table in traders' minds, the sector has given back recent gains despite real supply concerns like attacks on Saudi infrastructure.
